title: Gate calibration on openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol: one of six cases reproduces
hypothesis: The loop has only ever calibrated cases on qoder/dfmodel, where five of six candidates failed to discriminate. A stronger reasoning model may fail where dfmodel does not, and a case that only reproduces on one model must not be run as a gate on the other.
measurement: openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol, gate repeats 5 per arm, smoke first. Frozen baseline = installed release 0.1.27-main.50ccdc87 (Pi fork 1.4.0-rotom.2, SoL-Pi 0.1.0-rotom.6); candidate = origin/main 35de9563. Per case: `loop gate --case <id> --smoke` (1 pair), then `loop gate --case <id> --repeats 5`. Artifacts under ~/.rotom/loop/gate-2026-11-10T07-40..08-11. Total 2,969,160 tokens across smoke and repeat runs (baseline 1,480,707 / candidate 1,488,453), estimated cost $2.00 by Pi's price table, which is an estimate and not a bill.
result: Smoke: 6 of 6 cases passed the score audit (both arms scored, every check boolean, no check read a file the fixture never observed), no run was voided. Baseline failures out of five: behavior-authorized-follow-through 0/5, behavior-status-is-not-authorization 0/5 (control), behavior-mixed-decision-ownership 5/5, behavior-export-symptom 0/5, behavior-scoped-read 0/5, behavior-verification-path 0/5 (conformance control). Admission: only behavior-mixed-decision-ownership reaches the 3/5 rule and enters loop/gate.json on gpt-6.1-sol; the other five are recorded as not-reproduced for this model, and the dfmodel records stay as they were. The admitted case is an open failure, not a fixed one: the candidate arm also fails 5/5, so a gate run on it reports `regressed` until an agent change addresses it. Nothing about the agent changed in this round, so this entry measures reproduction only.

title: Field comparison of the default model: gpt-6-astra on odd days, gpt-6.1-sol on even days (28 days)
hypothesis: Published per-model v2 rates differ by more than sampling noise (openai-codex/gpt-6-astra 5.3 vs openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol 10.2 per 100 turns in the 28-day window), but a person chooses the model per task, so the difference may be task selection rather than model quality. Randomising the default by day removes that choice for the sessions that never switch.
measurement: Original dates 2026-11-11..2026-12-08 are void: the default-switch protocol was not operating. The 2026-11-11 read-only audit inspected only shell invocation lines, settings keys and filesystem times, not arm outcomes or adherence. Before reading experiment-period results, the corrected protocol is pre-registered: let L be the local date of the first verified successful launchd run. Day 1 is L+1; the inclusive 28-day window is L+1..L+28. The day-3 adherence-only check is L+3; if adherence is below 50%, stop and Ask. While activation is unconfirmed, weekly.json has experiment.restartPending=true and reports no arm counts. After user activation and log/settings readback, register the actual start/end dates and clear that flag. Assignment remains calendar-date parity, not experiment-day parity: odd dates openai-codex/gpt-6-astra, even dates openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol; thinking is high. Only sessions that start on that day's default and do not switch are eligible. Decision rule unchanged: compare v2/100 turns with 95% intervals; a difference counts only if the 95% interval of the difference excludes zero. Recompute after dropping each arm's largest-v2 session; a conclusion that disappears is sensitive, not robust. No arm outcome is read before the corrected window closes.
result: Protocol not operating as of 2026-11-11: no ~/.zshrc invocation of set-default-model.sh was found; settings still selected qoder/ultimate, thinking high, with mtime 2026-11-08T02:44:48.728361-08:00 (10:44:48Z), before the intended start. This establishes that the scheduled default switch was not successfully maintained; it does not establish what any individual session actually used. No session outcomes or adherence were inspected in this audit. A launchd plist for 00:01 local plus RunAtLoad and a private log wrapper were generated locally, not loaded by the agent. Await user activation and successful log/settings verification before setting L. This correction changes only scheduling/dates, not thresholds, assignment or analysis. Historical install-switch metadata is not an experimental start date. Closed 2026-11-11 by user decision: the comparison is cancelled and the user selects the model themselves. No valid experiment-period data was ever produced: the switch protocol never ran under the experiment, no arm outcome or adherence check was read, and the window was never opened, so L is undefined. The parity defaults, the weekly arm section, the adherence check and the harvest experiment view are removed; the weekly report keeps the per-model v2 split as observed data only.

title: 28-day harvest baseline: per-model v2 with intervals, sensitivity, task size and version layers
hypothesis: The loop reported a v2 rate per model as a single number and a weekly trend that mixed models, so a one-session outlier or a model that only gets small tasks could look like a product-quality change. Before starting the field comparison the window needs a baseline with its uncertainty and its selection bias visible.
measurement: No model calls. `npm --prefix rotom/evals run loop -- harvest --days 28 --experiment default-model` over ~/.pi/agent/sessions: 715 sessions, 1,678 incidents, 240 files outside the window, 706 artifact-store and 59 deep-directory subtrees skipped. Output stays in ~/.rotom/loop/harvest-2026-11-10T08-25-42-714Z.
result: Weekly v2 per 100 turns: W42 6.9, W43 7.8, W44 2.9, W45 5.4, W46 8.0. Per model with 95% Poisson bands: gpt-6-astra 5.3 (4–6.5, 1,314 turns), dfmodel 6.7 (5–8.4, 940), gpt-6.1-sol 10.2 (8.1–12.3, 901), gpt-5.6-sol 2.2 (0.9–3.5, 498), claude-opus-5-5 2.1 (239). Sensitivity: dropping the session with the most v2 events moves gpt-6.1-sol from 10.2 to 7.7 and dfmodel from 6.7 to 6.5, so about a quarter of sol's apparent rate is one conversation. Task size: median user turns per session 3–4 for all three main models; median tool calls per user turn 13.3 (astra), 27 (gpt-6.1-sol), 33.7 (dfmodel) — the harder, tool-heavy sessions do go to dfmodel and gpt-6.1-sol, which is the bias the field comparison has to control. Per product version: 0.1.27 4.3 (723 turns), 0.1.27-tps.1 7.5 (549), 0.1.26 6.6 (423), 0.1.27-main.0d90623 16.6 (302), 0.1.27-main.50ccdc87 14.3 (70); 167 of 715 sessions stay `unknown`. Per SoL-Pi version: 670 of 715 sessions are `unknown` because nothing records the loaded SoL-Pi version per session, and the rest resolve through older archive paths only. This is a baseline, not an improvement claim.
